title: Milky Way shines over snowy La Silla
caption: The Milky Way over a snowy La Silla Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Winter has come to ESO's La Silla Observatory, and above it the plane of the Milky Way slants across the frame in a spray of stars. Reading from right to left, the domes belong to the ESO 3.6-meter telescope, then the 3.58-meter New Technology Telescope (NTT), then the ESO 1-meter Schmidt telescope, and finally the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope, whose dome carries a layer of snow.

La Silla sits on the edge of the Atacama Desert at an altitude of 2400 meters, far from the lit-up cities of northern Chile. After sunset its skies turn pitch-black, and that darkness makes it one of the best places for astronomy.

Even a site this high, dry and remote gets weather. In the winter months snow can blanket the peak and the telescope domes. The high ESO sites see both hot and cold temperatures over the year and at times face harsh conditions.

understand.summary: A ground-based landscape photograph by José Francisco Salgado for ESO, taken in visible light. The colors are those the camera recorded.
understand.eye: A camera exposure collects more light than the eye, so the Milky Way appears fuller and brighter than it would to someone standing on the mountain.

explore: Next to the dome of the ESO 3.6-meter telescope is the small dome of the Coudé Auxiliary Telescope, which is no longer in use. Between it and the NTT are the observatory's water tanks. ESO Photo Ambassador José Francisco Salgado took the photograph.
alt: Wintry telescope domes on a mountaintop, one carrying snow, with the band of the Milky Way slanting across the starry sky above.
